newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell-Citgo starts new crude unit, coker.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell-Citgo starts new crude unit, coker.

text.p: Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co started up a $1.1-billion upgrade at its Houston refinery Wednesday afternoon, with the facility now running near design capacity of 235,000 barrels per day (bpd).
"The expansion is complete and we're operating near design capacity," a Citgo official said.
A new crude distillation unit and delayed coker, as well as revamped existing units, allows the refinery to process more heavy sour crude from Venezuela.
The refinery is now running Venezuelan BCF-17-API gravity crude, the official said.
The expansion was expected to be up last Sunday, but refinery officials ran into vibration problems with the compressor and other glitches.
Traders noted that some of the heavy sour crude that the refinery was expected to begin processing hit the market last week, prompting speculation about problems at the facility.
The upgrade is part of a Venezuelan crude oil supply agreement that will give Citgo, the domestic unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA, a 40 percent stake in the refinery.
